title.narrative: Ethiopia Lowlands Drought Anticipatory Action for March, April, and May 2025 Season

description.narrative: Project Objective: The anticipatory action proposed by WFP aims to prevent the humanitarian crisis and food insecurity anticipated in southern pastoral lowland areas of Oromia and Southern regions due to forecasted below-normal rain during March, April and May 2025 season.In drought anticipatory action, direct feed distribution provides immediate relief by delivering feed directly to livestock keepers, ensuring rapid response and quality control, especially in remote areas with weak markets. However, it can be costly and limit choice. In contrast, voucher-based feed distribution empowers livestock keepers to purchase feed from local markets, stimulating the local economy and offering flexibility, but may face challenges where markets are underdeveloped, or prices fluctuate. However, the voucher scheme will provide a chance to pursue a hybrid approach and enable a flexible optimization of the actions, increase effectiveness by balancing the strengths of both methods based on regional market conditions in the target areas. Moreover, the voucher scheme will engage the local feed suppliers as it brings effective demand through enhancing the purchasing power of households through vouchers Project Approach: WFP will implement a two-pronged strategy to achieve the above objectives: 1) Dissemination of EW messages and advisory and EW system strengthening–timely information dissemination will be implemented through DRMBs to vulnerable communities in a total of 17 woredas Oromia region. EW system strengthening in a total of 37 Woredas in the Southern Region. This will enable communities to foresee and make all possible efforts including their own traditional early action mechanisms to minimize the impact of the anticipated drought. 2) Livestock feed vouchers distribution to resource-constrained households (those with less than 6 tropical livestock units (TLU)) of the Public Safety Net Programme (PSNP) caseload for lean season support in prioritized four woredas of Oromia region only to safeguard their critical livestock assets over the dry window. The core activities include:Geographical prioritization and targeting of the most vulnerable woredas. EW Information dissemination of relevant messages in the local language of the Oromia region through various accessible media/communication outlets.Establishment and training of EW committeesFeed Voucher distribution - distribute feed vouchers to targeted households, allowing them to purchase feed from local suppliers to maintain their core breeding stock. This will enable households to maintain their food subsistence and rebuild their livestock assets after the drought. WFP will work in partnerships with FAO, DRMB, Cooperating partners and farmer cooperatives/ traders.Total Budget: 1.47 million USD.Expected Outcomes: EW messages and advisories disseminated to targeted households Trained and established early warning committeesReduced vulnerability for and impact of drought-related shocks among pastoral householdsEnhanced capacity and experience of local institutions (DRMBs) to provide gender and age responsive early warning and advisory servicesIn drought anticipatory action, direct feed distribution provides relief by delivering feed to livestock keepers, ensuring rapid response and quality control, especially in remote areas with weak markets. However, it can be costly and limit choice. In contrast, voucher-based feed distribution empowers livestock keepers to purchase feed from local markets, stimulating the local economy and offering flexibility. It may face challenges where markets are underdeveloped, or prices fluctuate. However, the voucher scheme will provide a chance to pursue a hybrid approach, increasing effectiveness by balancing the strengths of both methods based on regional market conditions in the target areas. Moreover, the voucher scheme will engage the local feed suppliers as it brings effective demand through enhancing the purchasing power of households through vouchers
